item.title: Surface Enhanced Anisotropy and Its Impacts on Massive Neutron Star Configurations in Einstein Gravity : Stability, Structure, and Multimessenger Consistency
item.description: arXiv:2611.09974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anisotropic neutron-star configurations are investigated within Einstein's General Relativity using a third-order polynomial equation of state, (p_r=A\rho+B\rho^2+C\rho^3), and the Buchdahl class-I metric ansatz, (e^{q(r)}=\frac{L(1+\tau r^2)}{L-\tau r^2}). Physically viable interior solutions are constructed and smoothly matched to the exterior Schwarzschild spacetime using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The stellar properties are examined through the matter distribution, pressure anisotropy, hydrostatic equilibrium, compactness, surface redshift, tidal deformability, causality, and dynamical stability. The energy density and radial and tangential pressures remain finite, positive, and monotonically decreasing throughout the interior, while the anisotropy vanishes at the centre and increases smoothly toward the surface. Generalized Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation confirms equilibrium through the balance of gravitational, hydrostatic, and anisotropic forces. Furthermore, adiabatic index satisfies the Chandrasekhar stability criterion, and both sound speeds obey the causality and Herrera cracking conditions. The compactness remains below the Buchdahl limit, with physically acceptable surface redshifts. The predicted maximum masses exceed the corresponding observed masses, with some configurations extending into the lower mass-gap region. The tidal deformabilities are consistent with multimessenger constraints from GW170817 and NICER. In addition, the theoretical mass-compactness relation and its prediction intervals show good agreement with observational estimates. Finally, Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis provides statistically reliable constraints on the tidal Love number, compactness, and perturbation parameter. These results establish a physically viable and observationally compatible framework for describing anisotropic neutron stars within General Relativity.
item.dc:creator: Ritabrata Biswas, Arpan Bhattacharya, Subhajit Pal

item.title: Periodic orbits and gravitational wave radiation of a phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld regular black hole Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate periodic orbits and gravitational wave radiation in the spacetime of an asymptotically flat regular black hole supported by a phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld scalar field. Starting from the timelike geodesic equations, we examine the effective potential and the characteristic circular orbits and construct periodic zoom--whirl trajectories. We further explore the sensitivity of orbital closure to small energy perturbations and examine the periastron advance of the $S2$ star around Sgr A$^*$ to assess possible constraints on the regular core parameter. The gravitational wave signals associated with representative periodic trajectories are then calculated within a quadrupole based numerical kludge approximation, considering both polarization modes. Particular attention is given to the influence of the regular core on orbital configurations and waveform characteristics, providing a complementary perspective on gravitational aspects of phantom Dirac--Born--Infeld regular black holes.
item.dc:creator: N. Heidari, A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, Iarley P. Lobo, V. B. Bezerra

item.title: Observational signatures of Bardeen black holes under nonlinear electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.09979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the shadow and optical appearance of the Bardeen black hole (BH) within nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED). Since photon propagation in nonlinear electromagnetic field can be equivalently described as null-geodesic motion in the effective metric induced by NLED, we derive the corresponding effective optical geometry of the NLED-Bardeen BH. Furthermore, by examining the horizon-photon sphere-shadow inequality, we demonstrate that the NLED-Bardeen BH does not satisfy the complete inequality chain. In addition, we investigate photon dynamics and the corresponding optical images generated by both thin disk and spherical accretion models. Increasing $g/M$ reduces the photon sphere radius and critical impact parameter, resulting in a more compact shadow and an inward shift of the emission peak. For the thin disk accretion model, photon trajectories are classified into direct emission, lensing ring, and photon ring components according to the corresponding impact parameter. We find that Model 1 exhibits three distinct intensity peaks, whereas Models 2 and 3 display two and one peaks. The systematic dependence of these features on the magnetic charge indicates that the NLED-Bardeen BH may exhibit observational signatures distinguishable from those of the Bardeen BH. In static spherical accretion, the intensity peaks near the critical impact parameter because of the enhanced optical path length, while infalling spherical accretion introduces an additional Doppler redshift that suppresses the observed intensity. These results indicate that the shadow size, ring structure, and intensity distribution can serve as potential observational signatures of NLED effects in the strong-field regime.
item.dc:creator: Haiyuan Feng, Dan-Dan Cui

item.title: Analogue Gravity: the Subcritical Case
item.description: arXiv:2611.10006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We focus on the subcritical case in Analogue Gravity for a subluminal dispersion relation, and investigate the problem of pair creation in the absence of an horizon analytically, for the subcritical white hole case. We limit our attention to weakly dispersive media. In particular, we take into account for simplicity the Corley model and adopt an approach inspired by quantum mechanics in the so-called overbarrier scattering. The presence of complex turning points is shown to play a fundamental role in allowing a mode conversion which would be absent in a naive WKB approach. We show that there is still a pair creation phenomenon, which, in the subcritical case, is non-Planckian and without a Hawking partner. Our fully analytical results are qualitatively in agreement with the literature at hand. Furthermore we confirm the existence of a critical regime betwen the subcritical and the transcritical ones where no pair creation occurs.
item.dc:creator: F. Belgiorno, S. L. Cacciatori, A. Vigan\`o

item.title: Scalable early warning for binary neutron-star mergers in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.10133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third-generation gravitational-wave observatories will observe binary neutron-star coalescences for hours before merger. Over these extended time windows, Earth's motion and the long signal durations make standard search methods computationally demanding for low-latency detection. We propose an approach based on short-time Fourier transforms and convolutional neural networks that implicitly marginalizes over extrinsic parameters, effectively reducing the search to the chirp mass. The network learns the signals' nonlinear time-frequency morphology, approximating the optimal Bayesian detection statistic. Using a large-scale campaign of simulated signal injections, we compare the network's performance with a GPU-optimized matched-filtering baseline for both the ET$\Delta$ and ET2L configurations of the Einstein Telescope and signal durations from approximately 25 minutes ($f_{\rm min} = 5$ Hz) to approximately 6 hours ($f_{\rm min} = 2$ Hz). The network achieves comparable detection sensitivity while reducing computational costs by over four orders of magnitude, bringing processing times from minutes to milliseconds. This efficiency paves the way for rapid early-warning alerts for multi-messenger astronomy in the third-generation detector era.
item.dc:creator: Martin Gerini, Rodrigo Tenorio, Davide Gerosa

item.title: Stealth scalars on prescribed dark-energy backgrounds: reconstruction, branch regularity, and perturbative bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.10231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reconstruct homogeneous stealth scalar fields on prescribed Friedmann--Lema\^itre--Robertson--Walker backgrounds with constant or evolving dark-energy equations of state. The scalar stress tensor vanishes, so the expansion history is supported by an independent background sector. Eliminating the self-interaction potential yields a Riccati equation for the scalar profile. We use it to distinguish exact stealthness from global regularity and from the stronger identification of a term in the scalar stress tensor with the prescribed dark-energy density. We prove that this sector-preserving identification is not dynamically invariant in a mixed flat constant-$w$ cosmology. For radiation-free $w$CDM backgrounds, a hypergeometric representation allows the regular and singular branches to be separated by a background-dependent threshold. At conformal coupling the reconstruction instead reduces to an exact comoving-distance quadrature, valid for arbitrary regular flat histories, including radiation. A CPL phantom-divide crossing does not singularize the background stealth equation, although the perturbations of the prescribed dark-energy sector require an independent treatment. The scalar--tensor description gives luminal high-frequency propagation under a positive effective Planck mass. If the field tracks its cosmological value locally without screening, Cassini constraints strongly suppress the corresponding late-time gravitational responses.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Blanco, Cuauhtemoc Campuzano, V\'ictor H. C\'ardenas, Giovany Cruz

item.title: Relativistic Simulations of Self-Gravitating Radiation Fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.10320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an approach for numerical simulations of pure radiation fluids within the general relativistic hydrodynamics framework. The approach models radiation as a self-gravitating perfect fluid with vanishing rest mass, enabling simulations of radiation fluids in strong-gravity spacetimes. Building on the existing relativistic hydrodynamics code Whisky, within the Einstein Toolkit framework, we introduce modifications to incorporate radiation fluids, including updates to the source terms, recovery scheme, and Riemann solvers. Modifications are validated using standard shock tube tests. We present results for radiation accretion onto a single black hole, as well as a photon star solution for radiation in unstable hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating both collapse and dispersion under perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Bing-Jyun Tsao, Pablo Laguna, Octavio Guerrero

item.title: Shallow-water black holes and lattice superradiance
item.description: arXiv:2611.10539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotating black holes can amplify waves that scatter off them, a process known as superradiance that fluid analogues bring into the laboratory. Separating the horizon's role from dissipation in the surrounding fluid remains difficult. Here we realise a rotating analogue black hole in a lattice fluid: a shallow-water vortex whose horizon is set by a topographic sill, so that the only sink lies behind a supercritical layer that lets nothing out. We measure superradiance as energy extraction: the flux at the horizon is outward for co-rotating waves whose pattern rotates more slowly than the horizon, and inward for faster waves, counter-rotating waves and a non-rotating hole. A scan over three lattice viscosities separates the extraction at the horizon, which is inviscid, from that of the viscous fluid inside the corotation radius: well below the band edge the horizon is the absorber; near the edge the viscous share is half at the operating viscosity and vanishes at the lowest. A drain-anchored horizon, as in water-tank experiments, gives the same signs. Our analysis gives insight into the mechanism of superradiance and offers a cheap, flexible platform for designing analogue-gravity experiments.
item.dc:creator: Antonino Flachi

item.title: Engineering a digital acoustic black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.10540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how to design and build an analogue black hole as a synchronous digital circuit. We define the sound speed, the flow and the horizon of such a circuit in terms of its own logic, and realise one on a field-programmable gate array, where the black hole is probed electrically with a signal generator and an oscilloscope. We measure the stability of the horizon, its causal cone, the ringdown and rotational superradiance. A single flipped bit inside the horizon leaks out by an amount that falls exponentially with depth. Digital circuits thus form a reconfigurable class of gravitational analogues and realise an analogue black hole as a cellular automaton.
item.dc:creator: Antonino Flachi

item.title: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe
item.description: arXiv:2611.10584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.
item.dc:creator: Nick E. Mavromatos, Sarben Sarkar

item.title: Generalized Second Law of Thermodynamics in $f(Q)$ Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the validity of the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics on the cosmological apparent horizon in $f(Q)$ symmetric teleparallel gravity, using the Wald-type entropy prefactor $Af_Q/4G$ together with a correction term derived directly from the modified Friedmann equations. We derive, and verify by explicit symbolic computation, a closed-form expression for the apparent horizon entropy in $f(Q)$ gravity and show that its time derivative combines with the matter entropy rate into a remarkably compact master formula, $T_A\dot S_{\rm tot} = 4\pi\dot H(\dot H f_Q + H\dot f_Q)/H^4$ (in units $8\pi G=1$), which correctly reduces to the known general-relativistic limit. We apply this formalism to three observationally viable $f(Q)$ models --- power-law, exponential, and logarithmic. We find that the GSL is satisfied throughout cosmic history for all three models, and relate this robustness to a general, theory-independent structural condition: for ordinary pressureless matter obeying the null energy condition, GSL validity reduces to the sign of $\dot H$, i.e., to the absence of a phantom crossing in the total effective expansion history. The geometric sector exhibits model-dependent energy conditions, power-law and exponential models violate only the strong condition, while the logarithmic model violates the null, weak, and dominant conditions for \(z>-1\), and the strong condition for \(z<3.84\).
item.dc:creator: Nadeem Azhar, Kayoomars Karami

item.title: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.10616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.
item.dc:creator: R. Casadio, A. Giusti, R. da Rocha

item.title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
item.description: arXiv:2611.10661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.
item.dc:creator: Kyriakos Destounis

item.title: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.10783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. Using the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon formalism, we construct a natural basis of independent tensors which are each canonically conjugate to precisely one multipole. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Scheopner, Felix Lichtner

item.title: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exact motion of a finite size object in curved spacetime is captured by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations. They associate a unique worldline, momentum, and spin to that object and determine the evolution of such in terms of its fully independent multipole moments. We provide a thorough review of this theory and show how to build it directly via a manifestly gauge invariant variational principle well-suited for effective descriptions of relativistic compact objects. We discuss conditions under which the covariant spin supplementary condition can be enforced and identify the natural basis of curvature tensors conjugate to the object's multipole moments.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Scheopner, Felix Lichtner

item.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.10880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_\lambda$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(\Omega,g,k=\lambda g)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $\lambda$ below a geometrically determined threshold $\alpha$, while vanishing $E_\lambda$ at $\lambda=\alpha$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_\lambda=0$ when $\lambda=\alpha$, then $(\Omega,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/\lambda$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Eric Ling, Annachiara Piubello

item.title: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
item.description: arXiv:2611.10933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.
item.dc:creator: Babak Vakili

item.title: Thermodynamic, Optical, and Wave Signatures of Charged Letelier AdS Black Holes with PFDM and Quintessence
item.description: arXiv:2611.10942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. We derive the curvature invariants, horizon temperature, entropy, electric potential, and horizon-based mass function, and analyze local thermal response and the associated extended-phase-space identities. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $\eta\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $\rho_{\rm PFDM}=-\beta/(8\pi r^3)$, so positive $\beta$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.
item.dc:creator: B. Eslam Panah, S. Gurtas Dogan, A. Guvendi, O. Mustafa

item.title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
item.description: arXiv:2611.11006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-V\theta)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $\kappa/2\pi$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8\pi GT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-V\theta)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-V\theta$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.
item.dc:creator: Roh-Suan Tung

item.title: Covariant Hamiltonian Gravity in Spherical Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.11099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building upon the covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, we construct the effective Einstein equation governing gravitational dynamics. For any prescribed one-parameter family of static, spherically symmetric metrics, this equation can be constructed such that the prescribed family constitutes their vacuum solutions. As an application, we construct generalized Vaidya solutions to the effective Einstein equation and show that the corresponding energy-momentum tensor takes precisely the standard Vaidya form. The results demonstrate that standard null dust sources can serve as matter source for dynamical black-hole geometries beyond general relativity, including regular black holes. Furthermore, this work suggests that quantum gravity corrections alone may not account for Hawking-like evaporation, as mass loss in the ingoing Vaidya solution necessarily requires a violation of the null energy condition within our effective framework.
item.dc:creator: Cong Zhang, Zhoujian Cao

item.title: Exceptional Points in Scalar Quasinormal Modes of Rastall String-Fluid Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study exceptional points (EPs) in scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of Rastall string-fluid black holes by adding a localized P\"oschl--Teller perturbation to the scalar potential, with the bump position $a$ and amplitude $\eb$ serving as independent controls. We solve the hyperboloidal problem with two-domain Chebyshev collocation and arbitrary-precision linear algebra, and use the complex discriminant, eigenvector coalescence, Jordan-chain residuals, square-root splitting and closed-loop mode exchange as complementary tests of defectiveness. For the regular $A=1$, $\eR=-1$ branch, the two-parameter search locates a resolution-stable second-order EP from $N=24$ to $N=60$, while constrained semidiscrete evolution gives the Jordan response $(C+Dt)e^{\ii\omega_{\rm EP}t}$. For the logarithmic $A=2$ branch, defective points occur in each finite truncation but their coordinates do not converge, so we make no continuum claim for this branch.
item.dc:creator: Ming Zhang, Xiao-Mei Wang, Ya-Nan Wang, Miao Wang, Lei Zhang, Xufen Zhang, De-Cheng Zou

item.title: Negative Dynamical Friction in Dark Matter Spikes around Rotating Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dark matter may affect extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) through orbital-energy exchange and a conservative metric response. Here we show that dark matter spikes around rotating massive black holes can drive negative dynamical friction, supplying orbital energy to secondary black holes on stable prograde circular orbits. The energy-gain region extends beyond the innermost stable circular orbit once the black-hole spin exceeds a model-dependent threshold. For an illustrative four-year inspiral with Milky Way--like halo parameters and mass ratio $q=10^{-5}$, the total dynamical-friction contribution produces a phase difference of order $10^2$ radians relative to vacuum. For the same system, the fixed-frequency environmental redshift correction is comparable in magnitude and opposite in sign to the first-order conservative self-force correction. Both environmental energy exchange and the conservative metric response are therefore essential to precision EMRI modeling.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xiong, Peng-Cheng Li, Bin Chen

item.title: Pushing the accuracy of the quasi-circular baseline for the SEOBNR family of models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened a new era of astronomy, with accurate modeling of binary black hole signals becoming increasingly important for source characterization and astrophysical inference as detector sensitivities improve. We present SEOBNRv5iHM, an updated quasi-circular, aligned-spin inspiral-merger-ringdown gravitational-waveform model with higher-order modes, constructed within the effective-one-body formalism and building upon SEOBNRv5HM. The improvements mainly concern the late inspiral and the merger-ringdown: we remove the non-quasi-circular corrections used in previous models and instead introduce a phenomenological intermediate region between the inspiral and the ringdown, which allows the ringdown attachment time to be chosen independently for each mode, including at the peak of the mode's amplitude. The model is calibrated and validated against 591 quasi-circular aligned-spin waveforms from the third Simulating eXtreme Spacetimes catalog. For the $(2,2)$ mode, when considering the maximum unfaithfulness against numerical relativity over a total mass range of 10-300$M_\odot$, SEOBNRv5iHM achieves a median of $4.25\times10^{-5}$, a factor of 4.5 below SEOBNRv5HM, and a factor of 3-8 below other semi-analytical models, with $84\%$ of cases below $10^{-4}$. For $M\ge150 M_\odot$, the median drops to $9.7\times10^{-6}$, comparable to the numerical-relativity surrogate NRHybSur3dq8. For polarization mismatches at inclination $\pi/3$, with modes up to $\ell_\mathrm{max} = 5$, the median maximum unfaithfulness is $4.2\times10^{-4}$, a factor of 2.6 below SEOBNRv5HM, 1.9 below IMRPhenomTHM, and 6-11 below the other semi-analytical models. Since spin-precessing and eccentric models are built on top of the quasi-circular, aligned-spin baseline, these improvements will make future SEOBNR models more accurate, reducing waveform systematics in upcoming analyses.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Foo, Alessandra Buonanno, H\'ector Estell\'es, Lorenzo Pompili

item.title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
item.description: arXiv:2611.11495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity. Finally, rotating Nariai data admit the required spacelike graph throughout the regular branch; an all-order tensor estimate yields smooth Kerr--de Sitter or rotating-Nariai rigidity for $a^2/r_0^2\leq1/8$, without assuming ambient axial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Ye Zhou

item.title: Quasinormal modes of a scale-dependent black hole in 5D spacetime with cosmological constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.11584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a scale-dependent black hole in five dimensions with a positive cosmological constant, considering i) scalar, ii) electromagnetic, and iii) Dirac perturbations. After deriving exact analytical solutions within the framework of scale-dependent gravity in five dimensions and selecting a different family of solutions (cf. \cite{Contreras:2019fwu}), we analyze the corresponding effective potentials (given by the lapse function) for each perturbation type. We employ a first-order approximation for the lapse function, as it closely matches the exact case for small $\varepsilon$. Since quantum corrections are expected to be small, our focus is on a relatively low range of the scale-dependent parameter $\varepsilon$. We confirm that the WKB semi-analytical approach can be used to compute the QNMs for these perturbations to the background geometry. We calculate the QNM frequencies for the classical case (for comparison) and for cases where the scale-dependent parameter $\varepsilon$, which quantifies deviations from General Relativity, is non-zero. The results are summarized in a series of tables and figures. Finally, we find that, regardless of the perturbation type, the solutions are stable, as the imaginary part of each QNM frequency is negative.
item.dc:creator: \'Angel Rinc\'on, Zden\v{e}k Stuchl\'ik

item.title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenb\"ock invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordstr\"om background.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Robledo, Yerko V\'asquez, P. A. Gonz\'{a}lez

item.title: Horizon-penetrating rotating black-hole configurations in VCDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.11775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A regular black-hole metric need not define a regular configuration of VCDM, whose preferred foliation is part of the gravitational solution. We construct stationary rotating, possibly charged configurations on the constant-auxiliary Einstein-Maxwell branch. Their Kerr-Newman and Kerr-Newman-de Sitter geometries carry nonzero constant-mean-curvature foliations that cross the future black-hole horizon and, in the de Sitter case, the future cosmological horizon. A horizon-regular flux formulation specifies the inner data and the distinct hyperboloidal and expanding asymptotic ends. Seventeen survey configurations are supplemented by a mean-flux scan at fixed four-geometry and paired flat/de Sitter comparisons down to $\kappa M = 0.01$, where $K_0 = 3\kappa$. Varying the flux changes the preferred-foliation shear without changing the background seen by standard test matter. The paired local lapse and shear differences have effective powers close to two over the computed range, with the lapse comparison requiring a fixed time normalization. Continuous residuals, geometric reconstructions, and selected grid comparisons test the numerical solutions. An exact lapse bound excludes zeros in the regular stationary exterior block with $\Delta_r > 0$. We distinguish singular finite-proper-distance endpoints from asymptotic trumpet ends and give conditional bounds on a stationary spacelike inner limit. A local cosmological interpretation requires additional matching assumptions; dynamical selection and the rotating interior endpoint are not determined by the stationary construction.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Felice

item.title: Quasinormal Modes of Black holes in the generalized Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution of $f(R)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze scalar, vector, and {axial} tensor perturbations in a Schwarzschild-type static spherically symmetric solution of modified $f(R)$ gravity. This solution differs from the Schwarzschild metric of general relativity through the presence of a linearly growing term and a logarithmic correction, and it depends on four integration constants. Using the higher-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation and an analytical method, we calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) for all three types of perturbations. Our results show that, for appropriately chosen parameter values, the QNMs closely match those of the Schwarzschild black hole. In particular, the model parameter $A$ produces a nonlinear increase in both the oscillation frequency and damping rate of ringdown gravitational waves. A similar effect arises for the parameter $\eta$ when $A$ is small, while for larger $A$ values the effects are opposite, where the scalar perturbations display a distinct deviation compared to the vector and {axial} tensor cases. Contour plots of QNMs in the parameter space support these findings. Finally, time-domain profiles are obtained to illustrate the dynamical evolution of the gravitational wave signal.
item.dc:creator: Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, Himanshu Chaudhary, Tiberiu Harko

item.title: Efficiency enhancement in the Unruh quantum Otto engine
item.description: arXiv:2611.11917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the efficiency enhancement of an Unruh quantum Otto engine (UQOE) composed of two initially unentangled Unruh-DeWitt (UDW) detectors. The two detectors have different accelerations and interact with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We choose a diagonal free Hamiltonian for the UQOE and define its work and heat with respect to the proper time of one of the detectors. Consequently, the coherence terms generated through the interaction with the scalar field do not directly contribute to the work and heat of the UQOE. Instead, the efficiency enhancement arises from the relative proper-time factor, which assigns different weights to the population changes of the two detectors. We then identify cyclic operating points that satisfy the conditions of initial-state passivity, cycle closure, and energy conservation. Their efficiency is higher than that of a conventional UQOE, and the state of the UQOE after the heat-absorption stage is separable. Finally, we study the effect of the separation between the two detectors on the engine efficiency. During the interaction of the two detectors with the field, increasing their separation reduces the generated entanglement; however, this separation enters the nonlocal coherence terms, thereby restricting the range of parameter settings compatible with cycle closure and influencing the achievable efficiency enhancement. Our results demonstrate that the UQOE can achieve enhanced efficiency even when its state after the heat-absorption stroke is separable, showing that entanglement generation is not a necessary condition for efficiency enhancement.
item.dc:creator: Yongjie Pan, Baocheng Zhang, Qingyu Cai

item.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Bayesian Inference for Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
item.description: arXiv:2611.11922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) pose a major challenge to Bayesian parameter inference because of their complex, highly multimodal likelihood surfaces. Locating narrow high-likelihood regions is particularly difficult without knowledge of the true source parameters, which is unavailable in real observations. We develop a deep-learning-assisted Bayesian inference framework that combines neural-network-guided parameter-space localization, particle swarm optimization, and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Applied to simulated six-month EMRI signals, the framework recovers posterior distributions in close agreement with reference MCMC analyses initialized near the true parameter values, without requiring such knowledge for initialization. Once the neural network has been trained, the complete inference pipeline takes approximately 10 hours per signal.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Jun Song, Zhong-Wu Xia, Wen-Hong Ruan, Zu-Cheng Chen, Hongwei Yu, Puxun Wu

item.title: Single and repetitive Penrose processes in genuine uncharged Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.11943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an analytical framework for the Penrose process in the genuine uncharged Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR0) black-hole spacetime within a Bertotti-Robinson (BR) electromagnetic vacuum, consistently linking particle decay, radial transport, thermodynamic states, and geometric reconstruction by distinguishing coordinate Killing energy from thermodynamic mass-generator energy and performing multibranch parameter mapping from thermodynamic states to background metric parameters. Furthermore, we present the analytical solution for the decay of equatorial massive neutral particles at a common radial turning point inside the ergoregion, the orbital accessibility criteria, and the six physical constraints required for a complete extraction event. Numerical calculations demonstrate that for both near-extremal and lower-spin inputs, in both single and repetitive Penrose processes, the net energy return on investment ($\eta_{\text{EROI}}$) and the rotational energy utilization efficiency ($\eta_{\text{EUE}}$) decrease with increasing external magnetic field, whereas the rotational energy reservoir consumption rate per unit incident energy ($\eta_{\text{thermo}}$) increases. For the inputs considered, the feasible domain and the upper bound of the initial magnetic field for single extraction are constrained by two boundary mechanisms: the obstruction of parent-particle infall and the loss of negative energy in the captured fragment. Finally, for repetitive extraction processes within the surveyed regime, all sequences terminate due to orbital accessibility obstructions, explicitly local-slope failure and far-field incident-branch closure, with the final black-hole state retaining most of its initial rotational energy reservoir. Moreover, the black-hole state evolves along a common integral curve independent of the parent particle's specific energy, which solely alters the sequence endpoint.
item.dc:creator: Ruo-Cen Wu, Hanjun Zou, Meng Xu, Yun-Long Zhang

item.title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. The critical curve's signed normal displacement factorizes as $\tilde u_n=\tilde F_{\mathrm K}\mathscr C$, where $\tilde F_{\mathrm K}$ depends only on the Kerr reference geometry and $\mathscr C$ is an explicit combination of optical metric deviations. The demagnification exponent, time delay, and azimuthal advance are evaluated at a common position angle on the observer screen. Intrinsic relations among the exact observables express the optical information shared by the curve, time delay, and azimuthal advance, while demagnification additionally depends on radial instability. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Peng Yan, Xiang-Qian Li, Xiao-Jun Yue

item.title: Next-to-next-to-leading gravitational radiation-reaction corrections to quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic compact binary orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.12093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the Lagrange method of variation of constants to compute the radiation-reaction (RR) corrections to the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic motion of compact binary systems at 4.5PN order, i.e., at next-to-next-to-leading order in the RR. We rely on the recent determination of the 4.5PN RR acceleration, in a general frame and in the center-of-mass frame, in harmonic coordinates. The non-local effects, due to the tails at 4PN order and to the gravitational-wave recoil at 4.5PN order, are carefully evaluated. Although the calculation is implemented differently in the quasi-elliptic and quasi-hyperbolic cases (different perturbation equations and choices of orbital parameters), we verify by analytic continuation that the results for the local effects are equivalent in the two cases.
item.dc:creator: Donato Bini, Luc Blanchet, Guillaume Faye, Andrea Geralico, Quentin Henry, Sara Rufrano Aliberti, Emeric Seraille

item.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.
item.dc:creator: Petr Jizba, Tereza Lehe\v{c}kov\'{a}

item.title: Gravity Without Absolutes
item.description: arXiv:2611.12489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By formulating his theory of universal gravitation in absolute space and time, Newton demonstrated the power of reductionism; it has been behind every major advance in physics since then. However, the lack of significant advances over the last half-century, together with unresolved problems in the dominant paradigms of physics and cosmology, suggest that holism may need to replace reductionism as the way forward. The ontological simplicity and historical significance of Newtonian gravity makes it the ideal theory for examining this possibility. Taking Newton's second law of motion to be the core of his theory, we show that its use within the reductionist framework of absolute space and time introduces an infinity of arbitrary solutions if used to describe $N$-body universes rather than subsystems within them. We show that Leibniz's principle of sufficient reason (PSR) eliminates the infinite arbitrariness and transforms the predicted nature of $N$-body universes; they are all shown to be unexpectedly interesting. An even greater change is enforced if one asks what principle could determine the number of particles in the universe. The PSR suggests it can only be infinite. We suggest that, in such a universe, correlation could replace causation while still giving the appearance that each state has been created by dynamical evolution from the past, whereas its actual explanation may lie entirely within the present state. While much work remains to develop these ideas into a viable theory, we are confident that it advances the case for holism.
item.dc:creator: Julian Barbour, Maria I. R. Louren\c{c}o

item.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.12683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the horizon electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics automatically satisfied, but also both the CR relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Xu Yan, Zili Mou, Yu Tian, Hongbao Zhang

item.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2611.12831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxi Wu, Elias R. Most

item.title: Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
item.description: arXiv:2611.12838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation. The analytic background yields exact constraints on the spectrum. At fixed azimuthal number $m$, the frequencies $\widehat{\omega}=r_0\omega$ are mirror symmetric about $\operatorname{Re}\widehat{\omega}=3\pi jm/2$, where $r_0$ is the throat radius and $j=J/r_0^2$ is the dimensionless angular momentum. Each multipole family depends on $m$ and $j$ only through $mj$ and three angular Chebyshev polynomials represent exactly the multipoles $L=|m|,|m|+1,|m|+2$. A conserved flux confines nonthreshold real quasinormal frequencies to the superradiant window $0<\omega/(m\Omega_-)<1$, where $\Omega_-=3\pi J/r_0^3$. For the sampled sectors $m=1,2,3$ and spins up to $j=19$, every converged frequency is damped and lies outside this window. Independent integration verifies the low-lying modes, while Kerr spectra provide a separate benchmark for the two-dimensional solver. A limiting radial equation explains why the computed mode frequencies approach the upper edge of the superradiant window with frequency offsets proportional to $(mj)^{-1/2}$ at large $mj$. A complete stability assessment requires further analysis of the unresolved scalar spectrum and of perturbations of the coupled metric-matter system.
item.dc:creator: Mark Sukaiti, Davide Batic, Denys Dutykh

item.title: Beyond $\Lambda$CDM: Probing Structure Growth and Observational Viability of Generalized ${f\,(Q , \mathcal{L}_{m})}$ Gravity
item.description:
arXiv:2611.12839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $f(Q, \mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity is a well-known extension of $f(Q)$ gravity, obtained through non-minimal or additive minimal coupling in the action's Lagrangian density. Background-level cosmography within this framework, along with comparisons to $\Lambda$CDM, has been the focus of prior studies. The present work considers a generalized power-law form of the additive minimal coupling, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m) = -Q^\mu + \alpha \mathcal{L}_m^{\,
u} +  eta$, from which the Hubble function $H(z)$ is derived through a novel parametrization. When $

Constraints on the model parameters are obtained from Observational Hubble Data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and three SNe Ia compilations (Pantheon+, Union3, DES-SN5YR), allowing their cosmographic effects to be examined. Beyond the background level, the perturbed field, Euler, and continuity equations are derived under non-conservation, and their impact on structure growth is studied through a joint analysis incorporating the $f\sigma_8$ probe. Bayesian evidence, computed relative to $\Lambda$CDM, shows that the model is favoured by background data in several cases, with moderate support for one realisation, whereas the inclusion of $f\sigma_8$ drives $

item.dc:creator: Raj Kumar Das, Sivasish Paul

item.title: Mapping of Spacetimes with Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.12857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gauge freedom in numerical relativity complicates the interpretation of simulation coordinates and the comparison of different descriptions of the same spacetime. We present a data-driven neural network method for learning coordinate maps from numerical metric data to a prescribed target gauge. The network is trained by matching the transformed source metric to the target metric, without assuming a functional form for the coordinate transformation. We first validate the method on analytical Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries, recovering known transformations up to the isometries of the target spacetime. We then apply it to numerical black hole evolutions in moving-puncture coordinates. For a non-spinning black hole, the learned map relates the time-dependent numerical metric to a stationary Schwarzschild metric in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates. For a spinning puncture, the method provides an approximate identification with a Kerr background despite departures from Kerr in the numerical spacetime. We use this identification to construct curvature perturbations and evolve them with the Teukolsky equation, obtaining waveforms that closely match those extracted from the full nonlinear simulation. These results demonstrate that learned coordinate maps can relate numerical spacetimes to analytical backgrounds, with potential applications to cross-code validation and black hole perturbation theory.
item.dc:creator: Estuti Shukla, David Radice, Rossella Gamba, Sebastiano Bernuzzi

item.title: Kasner Exponents from the Bouncing Singularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.31699v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermal two-point functions of holographic CFTs can probe the black hole singularity. When a bouncing geodesic exists, the correlator at leading order in $1/N$ develops a singularity $G(t, \vec{x}=0) \propto (t_c-t)^{-2\Delta+b_t}$, where $\Delta$ is the scaling dimension of the operator. We show that the additional exponent $b_t$ is determined by the Kasner exponents near the singularity. From the wave reflected off the singularity, which gives an exponentially small term in the large-frequency retarded correlator, we derive the formula $b_t=(d-1) \max \left( \frac{p_i-p_t}{1-p_t}, \frac{1}{2} \right)$ for planar black branes in AdS$_{d+1}$, where $p_t$ and $p_i$ are the Kasner exponents of the time and spatial directions. We compare our formula with the numerical values of \v{C}eplak and Valach. It reproduces the relation that they proposed for a special class of black branes. For more general black branes, where no formula had been found, our formula agrees with most of their numerical data and fits them much better than the extension of their relation. We also give predictions for $b_t$ in theories where the Kasner exponents are known, but $b_t$ has not been computed.
item.dc:creator: Hyunwoo Oh

item.title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.07331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an algebraic classification of canonical single-field inflationary dynamics using an exact depressed cubic equation for the inflaton velocity. Its root structure identifies a branch-swap boundary distinct from the limiting boundary of downhill motion, where ultra-slow-roll inflation naturally emerges. Independently, the conservation of momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation in the long-wavelength limit provides a criterion for the growth or decay of the gauge-invariant difference between comoving and uniform-density curvature perturbations. Combining these criteria, we construct a unified dynamical chart in terms of the Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, illustrating its applicability to constant-roll inflation and simple toy models. Our classification shifts the emphasis from assigning models to fixed categories toward understanding the dynamical regimes traversed by inflationary trajectories and their implications for primordial perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Jinn-Ouk Gong, Wei-Chen Lin

item.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
item.description: arXiv:2611.09216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $\theta_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $\xi_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei Chen, Marie Cassing, Paramvir Singh, Luciano Rezzolla

item.title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
item.description: arXiv:2611.09988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.
item.dc:creator: Ankit C. Khunt, Swagat S. Mishra

item.title: A Free-Field Realization of Boundary Symmetries in Discrete Jackiw--Teitelboim Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a finite-periodic Miura free-field realization of the classical Virasoro--dilaton sector relevant to sl(2,R) Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Starting from a single logarithmic Cartan field, we use the established discrete Miura map and its free-field Poisson bracket to construct the lattice spin-two current. The dilaton is then realized as a periodic composite of the same Cartan variables, selected by an inhomogeneous difference equation and its monodromy condition. This construction yields an explicit induced mixed Poisson bracket without postulating an independent dilaton bracket. We examine the associated transfer problem and quadratic adjoint invariant, and test the finite Fourier algebra against the continuous Virasoro--dilaton transformation, in which the dilaton has conformal weight minus one. The construction supplies a free-field counterpart of the JT boundary transformation laws; it does not by itself identify the Miura Poisson structure with the canonical BF boundary-charge algebra.
item.dc:creator: H. T. \"Ozer, Ayt\"ul Filiz

item.title: Gravitational Production of Non-minimally Coupled Vector Dark Matter in Warm Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2611.10090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the purely gravitational production of a massive vector dark matter with a non-minimal coupling to the Einstein tensor, $\xi G_{\mu\nu}X^\mu X^\nu$, in warm inflation. The background, $V=\lambda\phi^4$ with a dissipation coefficient linear in temperature, is constrained by CMB observations and parametrized by the dissipation ratio $10^{-4}\le Q_0\le1$. We consider both unavoidable production channels: freeze-in from the Standard Model bath through graviton exchange, and cosmological gravitational particle production (CGPP). For freeze-in, we compute the scattering amplitudes including the contact interaction induced by $\xi$, which enhances the production of light dark matter through the longitudinal mode and suppresses that of heavy dark matter through destructive interference. For CGPP, the slow-roll parameter is not small during warm inflation, which enhances the production of light dark matter by up to three orders of magnitude relative to cold inflation. Combining both channels, CGPP excludes most of the light freeze-in branch, leaving $m_X\lesssim2.4\times10^{-5}$ GeV, a narrow window around $10^{10}$ GeV for strong dissipation, and $m_X\gtrsim10^{14}$--$10^{15}$ GeV. Only the heavy branch remains viable for all $|\xi|\lesssim1$.
item.dc:creator: Phongsakorn Sereewat

item.title: Baby Universes Nucleate by Hiding Observers from the Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.10112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Observers are expected to be essential to describe closed universes, but their description within a conventional holographic theory remains challenging. We study two double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models coupled by a four-parameter interaction, which includes a generalized Maldacena-Qi coupling, in a state that contains an observer, represented as a particle. With a heavy particle inside, the wormhole connecting the two systems can only grow. Rare products of Hamiltonian strings cancel the string of the particle: a closed baby universe then carries the observer, and the wormhole, now empty, recovers discrete states of finite length. The energy gained by the empty wormhole pays for the entropy of the observer, in a first-order transition whose latent heat is the transition temperature times this entropy. Krylov complexity, which measures the wormhole length, drops at the transition and thus detects from the boundary the emergence of the baby universe, whose boundary description is actively debated. The boundary also loses the Holevo information about the microstates of the observer, which the baby universe carries.
item.dc:creator: Sergio E. Aguilar-Gutierrez, Takato Mori

item.title: Emergent de Sitter Universes in Non-Hermitian Holography
item.description: arXiv:2611.10121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS), regular black holes whose interiors evolve into nonsingular, expanding de Sitter (dS) cosmologies. Our construction relies on non-Hermitian holography, where violations of the null energy condition allow the interior geometry to undergo a smooth bounce and approach a late-time dS attractor. The cosmology emerges dynamically behind a single event horizon, extending to a spacelike future boundary, $\mathcal I^+$, without introducing auxiliary branes or gluing distinct geometries. This provides a novel setting to explore the connections between three complementary holographic perspectives: a non-Hermitian conformal field theory (CFT) at the AdS boundaries, a putative Euclidean CFT at $\mathcal I^+$ (dS/CFT), and observer-centered static-patch holography. Remarkably, observables anchored at the AdS boundaries reveal concrete connections with these complementary notions of dS holography. Our construction thus offers a new holographic laboratory for systematically exploring how future-boundary and static-patch descriptions of dS quantum gravity may emerge within the established setting of AdS/CFT.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Are\'an, Suman Das, David Garcia-Fari\~na, Juan F. Pedraza

item.title: Holographic warped CFTs on AdS$_3$, parity violation and unitarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider recently introduced boundary conditions for General Relativity on AdS$_3$, whose canonical generators span the warped conformal algebra, in the case of the Einstein-Hilbert action supplemented by parity-odd terms that do not modify the field equations in vacuum. The canonical generators are shown to acquire nonlinear contributions, and their algebra remains being the semidirect sum of Virasoro and $u(1)$ Kac-Moody, but with shifted central extensions. Thus, for suitable values of the parity-odd coupling, the Kac-Moody level can be nonnegative ($k_\text{KM}\geq 0$), admitting unitary representations. Nevertheless, requiring the black hole entropy to be nonnegative, implies $k_\text{KM}\leq 0$, in agreement with the established understanding of holographic warped CFTs. Compatibility of both requirements (entropy and unitarity) then singles out the case $k_\text{KM}=0$. However, the field equations degenerate in this case, which can be amended by imposing vanishing torsion as a constraint. The theory then precisely becomes Topologically Massive Gravity (TMG) at the chiral point, suggesting the extension of our boundary conditions to accommodate nontrivial logarithmic branches.
item.dc:creator: Kristiansen Lara, Ricardo Troncoso

item.title: The Ghost and Its Secret Partner
item.description: arXiv:2611.10128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The propagator of a ghost field acquires a pair of first-sheet complex conjugate poles above the multi-particle threshold. We show that this pole structure reveals the existence of a hidden asymptotic composite field -- the ghost's secret partner -- that remains coupled to the ghost asymptotically. This coupling induces persistent interference between the negative-norm one-particle state and the positive-norm composite-particle state. We analyze this phenomenon in four-derivative theories, in particular quadratic gravity, where the quantum dynamics prevents the spin-two ghost from appearing as an isolated asymptotic excitation. Although our results do not yet rule out observable negative probabilities, they may provide a dynamical basis for alternative amplitude prescriptions or superselection rules usually chosen or imposed ad hoc in theories with indefinite-norm vector spaces.
item.dc:creator: Luca Buoninfante

item.title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
item.description: arXiv:2611.10203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a systematic expansion of dynamical black hole solutions in a class of five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton theories that are holographically dual to nearly critical, strongly coupled four-dimensional field theories. The expansion is motivated, through dimensional reduction, by the large-D limit of pure gravity, where D is the number of spacetime dimensions. At leading nontrivial order, the Einstein equations reduce to a closed set of non-relativistic hydrodynamic equations in four dimensions, as first shown in our previous letter; these equations generalize the large-D effective theory of black branes. We derive the thermodynamics and hydrodynamics of the system from black hole thermodynamics and the holographic dictionary, and show that the energy-momentum tensor extracted from the near-boundary geometry is conserved precisely when the effective equations hold. We analyze planar, cylindrical, and spherical domain walls between coexisting phases, as well as non-equilibrium steady-state walls with nonzero momentum flux. We also show how the near-horizon geometry can be completed by a holographic flow to an asymptotically AdS5 region. Finally, as an application to the confinement-deconfinement transition of Yang-Mills theory, we construct the domain wall between the confined and deconfined phases in improved holographic QCD, compute its surface tension, and compare it with recent lattice results.
item.dc:creator: Matti J\"arvinen, Leonardus B. Putra, Dorin Weissman

item.title: Polarization Signatures of Magnetic Reconnection Bubbles near Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.10525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the observed horizon-scale polarization variability in multi-epoch Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) data, we develop a time-dependent general relativistic polarized ray-tracing framework to study how localized magnetic reconnection near a black hole imprints itself on synchrotron polarization. We model the reconnection phenomenologically as a transient magnetic bubble. While keeping the underlying spacetime, emission prescription, and polarization transport scheme unchanged, the bubble weakens the local ordered field, reorganizes its geometry, induces a conservative local kinematic response, and relaxes through a finite magnetic-memory prescription. We explore how the key bubble parameters control the recovery of the magnetic-field strength, the spatial spreading of the disturbed region, the persistence of the post-reconnection imprint, and the resulting polarization signatures. Perturbations dominated by different magnetic-field components produce distinct polarized morphologies, EVPA evolution, and Stokes-(Q, U) trajectories: azimuthal perturbations favor outward EVPA shifts, radial perturbations favor inward shifts, and vertical perturbations mainly suppress the polarized intensity. For the illustrative M87^*-like cases, the phase evolution of the \beta_2 polarization coefficient further traces how localized magnetic reconfiguration contributes to the global EVPA twist of the ring. These results show that horizon-scale polarization variability can provide a sensitive diagnostic of localized magnetic restructuring and that the present framework offers a physically transparent way to interpret time-dependent polarimetric signatures in future EHT observations.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Xiang Huang, En-Wei Liang

item.title: Constraining Cosmic Deceleration using the Solar System
item.description: arXiv:2611.10596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate whether Solar System dynamics can provide independent constraints on the present day cosmological deceleration parameter $q_0$, offering a complementary approach to conventional cosmological probes. By relating cosmic acceleration to a weak Hooke type radial perturbation, we derive bounds using planetary perihelion precession, trans-Neptunian objects, and Oort cloud dynamics. We obtain relatively robust planetary bounds of $|q_0|\lesssim 10^9$, while the outer Solar System yields potentially stronger, albeit more model dependent, constraints approaching $10^5$. Through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses, we explore the statistical robustness of these estimates and their dependence on orbital measurements. Finally, we demonstrate how future precision astrometry and outer planet missions could improve these limits by several orders of magnitude, establishing Solar System dynamics as a complementary laboratory for probing cosmological acceleration.
item.dc:creator: Paridhi Jain, Oem Trivedi, Maxim Khlopov, Jackson Levi Said, Maxim Krasnov

item.title: Self-bound quantum dark fermion stars: saturation, a coupling-capped maximum mass, and tidal signatures of a vector dark sector
item.description: arXiv:2611.10662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: I show that a dark sector whose fermions couple to both a scalar and a vector mediator saturates in close analogy with nuclear matter: the energy per particle develops a minimum at finite density, cold dark matter of this kind is self-bound, and its stars, computed here in full general relativity, possess the sharp surfaces of strange quark stars. Saturation makes the maximum stellar mass a property of the Lagrangian rather than an inheritance of the Chandrasekhar scaling: it rises eightfold across the saturation window, which a critical vector coupling closes, so the theory caps its own maximum mass, at $3.9\,M_\odot$ for a fermion of $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the fiducial saturation density, a ceiling shared by the whole family of couplings rather than by any single parameter set. Metastable couplings support two disconnected stable families, one dilute and gravitationally bound, the other dense and self-bound. The quantum-pressure correction, confined by saturation to a surface layer a few Compton wavelengths thick, governs the smallest dark nuggets whilst shifting stellar masses by less than one part in $10^{21}$. A $1.4\,M_\odot$ member of the fiducial family has a radius of $13.3\,\mathrm{km}$, a compactness of $0.155$, and a tidal deformability of $1.6\times 10^{3}$, almost an order of magnitude above the measured neutron-star value, so at a given particle mass and couplings a single well-measured inspiral distinguishes these stars from neutron stars and from their scalar-only counterparts, whilst the deformability surviving at the maximum mass separates them, in principle, from black holes.
item.dc:creator: Ilidio Lopes

item.title: Is Dark Energy Inhomogeneous?
item.description: arXiv:2611.11094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The discovery of dark matter deficient galaxies motivates a fundamental question: Could sufficiently large regions of the Universe be deficient in dark energy as well? We investigate this possibility by developing a phenomenological framework that distinguishes genuine dark energy deficiencies from ordinary matter voids through nonlinear expansion, coherent peculiar velocities and density-momentum correlations.
