We show that a $10\%$ dark energy deficiency can suppress the expansion of a representative nonlinear void by approximately $2.7\%$, generating peculiar velocity residuals of order $60$-$100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across scales of $30$-$50\, Mpc$. Intriguingly, we find that deficiencies of order $20\%$ extending over several hundred megaparsecs could also influence the locally inferred Hubble constant, potentially contributing to the $H_0$ tension, subject to stringent isotropy and dynamical consistency constraints. We identify observational strategies involving DESI, Rubin, peculiar velocity surveys, and cosmic void catalogues, opening a new avenue for testing whether the dark energy driving cosmic acceleration is truly homogeneous.
item.dc:creator: Oem Trivedi, Abraham Loeb

item.title: Stanley Deser 19th March 1931 - 21st April 2023
item.description: arXiv:2611.11323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stanley Deser was Ancell Professor Emeritus at Brandeis University and Visiting Professor at the California Institute of Technology. He was a world-renowned theoretical physicist whose accomplishments include the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formulation of general relativity, supergravity with Zumino, the dynamics of flat space with Jackiw and 't Hooft and many other contributions to the quantum theory of gravity. In the 1980s he was instrumental in securing National Science Foundation approval of the LIGO gravitational wave experiment against much opposition. He was awarded the Einstein Medal in 2015 for important contributions to general relativity, in particular the development of the ADM formalism. Other awards include: The Dannie Heineman Prize 1994; Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences 1994; Honorary Member of the Torino Academy of Sciences 2001; Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences 1979, Fellow of the American Institute of Physics.
item.dc:creator: M. J. Duff, K. S. Stelle

item.title: What an Observer Reads off a Holographic Screen
item.description: arXiv:2611.11356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What does an observer read off a holographic screen that is an array of qubits rather than a surface? In the generalized holographic principle the interaction between two separable systems acts on such a screen as a weighted sum, up to an overall prefactor, of commuting observables with values plus and minus one. When the weights are nonnegative and the prefactor is one and the joint eigenspaces are lines, everything a probe reads off the spectrum depends only on the list of weights, which we call the profile. On the screen with equal weights summing to one the running dimension read by a diffusion probe falls short of two at unit time by at most twice the reciprocal of the number of qubits; a geometric profile gives instead, through its level count, a plateau of any positive height. An observer correlates sets of qubits; its readout carries a profile at a given weighting when the levels it reads, counted with multiplicity, are those of a screen with one weight per set. We prove that a readout carries a profile at every weighting exactly when the distinct nonzero traces of its qubits are linearly independent over the field with two elements, the trace of a qubit being the list of sets that contain it; such a readout is a partition of the qubits it covers up to an invertible recoding, and a dependent one carries a profile only on finitely many proper linear subspaces of weightings. Refining a grouping without end builds a tower whose boundary is a profinite set and hence a condensed set, on which a strictly positive compatible profile separates the locally constant functions by a distance. Applications certify probabilistic and strong contextuality and give the leading shortfall of the distance between the poles of the fuzzy sphere; in a model of monogamous entanglement the pairs that weight-one threads representing operational ER=EPR can occupy at once are exactly the partial matchings.
item.dc:creator: Kenan Oggad, James F. Glazebrook, Chris Fields

item.title: Proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC
item.description: arXiv:2611.11760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a general proof of the R\'{e}nyi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Vacuum energy interacting with dark matter and dark radiation: alleviating the $H_0$-$S_8$ seesaw
item.description: arXiv:2611.11835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extensions of $\Lambda$CDM that raise $H_0$ with additional energy before recombination, such as dark radiation and early dark energy (EDE), also raise $S_8$. We study whether a late-time energy exchange between the vacuum and the dark sector can offset this increase. The coupling rate scales as $\bar m H^{\alpha}$ and is negligible before recombination for $\alpha \le -2$; the energy is transferred along the four-velocity of geodesic cold dark matter, so the dark matter produced by the vacuum carries no density perturbation and slows the growth of structure. We add the exchange to dark radiation ($\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM) and to a one-parameter EDE model ($\bar m$EDE), and constrain the models with Planck 2018, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ data (CBS), and with the SH0ES calibration added (CBSH) to test the exchange when $H_0$ is held at a high value. For CBS the posteriors favour an energy flow from the vacuum into dark matter at 1.8-2.7$\sigma$, and the exchange lowers $S_8$ by 0.02-0.08 but does not raise $H_0$: $\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM gives $H_0 = 68.83 \pm 0.91$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, 3.1$\sigma$ below SH0ES. For CBSH the exchange removes the increase of $S_8$ caused by dark radiation, giving $S_8 = 0.800 \pm 0.016$ at $H_0 = 71.34 \pm 0.70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, and about a third of that caused by EDE for $\alpha = -2$, with the coupling at 1.1-2.0$\sigma$. The reduction of $S_8$ is concentrated at $z \lesssim 0.3$: at the redshifts probed by KiDS-Legacy the lensing amplitude decreases by only 1-2%, the shear $\chi^2$ of the dark-radiation models changes by less than 3, and the exchange reduces but does not remove the excess shear $\chi^2$ of EDE. A late-time exchange can therefore offset part of the $S_8$ increase of early-time solutions, but it does not ease the Hubble tension, and current data do not require it.
item.dc:creator: Li-Yang Gao, She-Sheng Xue, Xin Zhang

item.title: Work needed to lift a mass in Schwarzschild spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.11879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the work needed to lift a mass from $r_2$ to $r_1$ in Schwarzschild spacetime in three ways. First we use a winch and a light rope. Then we use a photon collision. Finally we let the mass decay into photons and reconstruct it at the higher radius. All three methods give the same local work at $r_1$, $W_1=mc^2[1-N(r_2)/N(r_1)]$, where $N(r)=\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$. Thus, independently of $r_1$, the work tends to $mc^2$ as $r_2$ approaches the horizon. The rope example also gives a useful general-relativistic version of a simple machine: a rope in equilibrium need not have equal local forces at its two ends. The redshift factor plays the role of the lever arm. For a real rope the energy conditions prevent the tension from decreasing with height, so this lever advantage is confined to the idealization. The examples are intended as teaching material for undergraduate relativity courses.
item.dc:creator: Anamta Asif, Andrzej Czarnecki

item.title: The shape and velocity of black hole coronas
item.description: arXiv:2611.11884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The first highly significant detection of the polarization of the X-rays from the Black Hole X-ray Binary Cygnus X-1 revealed surprisingly strong polarization parallel to its radio jet. The observation is now commonly interpreted as resulting from the Comptonization of some lower frequency seed photons in a laterally extended corona. The emitting plasma is likely moving along the jet axis with a sizable fraction beta of the speed of light, amplifying the polarization degree. In this letter we address the question of how laterally extended the corona actually needs to be to account for the observations, and we calculate the required outflow velocities of velocity-stratified coronas as a function of the stationary-frame aspect ratio h=H/2R of cylindrical coronas of height H and radius R. We find that models with h lesser equal 0.8 and beta=0.5-0.9 at the top of the corona can give both the observed photon index of Gamma=1.6 and the observed 4% polarization parallel to the symmetry axis. We do not find suitable solutions for larger h. Given the constraints on h, we discuss the likely size of the corona, emphasizing that compact coronas close to the black hole are preferred as they can tap more efficiently into the gravitational energy and the rotational energy of the black hole, and are less exposed to their own emission reprocessed in the optically thick portion of the accretion flow.
item.dc:creator: Henric Krawczynski (Washington University in St. Louis), Kun Hu (Washington University in St. Louis), Sohee Chun (Washington University in St. Louis)

item.title: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight
item.description: arXiv:2611.11920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We complete a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) in the mathematical framework of Half-Sided Translations and Modular Inclusions (HST/HSMI) removing an assumption that applied to previous proofs. Here we establish a theorem, which when translated to a physical setting implies that the relative entropy comparing the state of fields outside a stationary black hole with a Hartle-Hawking (HH) state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. Previous proofs only applied when a purification with finite null energy was available. We also obtain a QNEC generalization in which the HH Hilbert space is replaced with one based on a weight which is plausibly of relevance to evaporating black holes in flat space.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Faulkner

item.title: Einstein--Yang--Mills Plane Waves: Uniqueness and an Exact Curvature Double Copy
item.description: arXiv:2611.12204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coleman found plane waves of Yang--Mills theory that are genuinely non-abelian in four dimensions and yet obey linear field equations, and G\"uven showed that they remain exact when gravity is included. We study these waves in $D$ dimensions. Coleman's profile, which is linear in the transverse coordinates, is singled out twice: up to gauge, it is the only profile with bounded energy density, and the only one for which the full Riemann tensor equals the color-contracted square of the Yang--Mills field strength that sources it. In anti-de Sitter space, we construct a closed-form family for every $D\geq4$; there, the full Riemann tensor cannot equal this color square. Waves whose transverse space is a sphere are always singular. In quadratic and Gauss--Bonnet gravity, a hyperbolic transverse space avoids this only if the waves defocus light or the higher-curvature terms become comparable to the Einstein term. All solutions extend, with changed coefficients, to generic gravity and gauge theories.
item.dc:creator: Metin Gurses, Tahsin Cagri Sisman, Bayram Tekin

item.title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.12282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.
item.dc:creator: Chian-Shu Chen, Feng-Li Lin

item.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Thakur, Yeunhwan Lim

item.title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.12482v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Qi Chen, Hai-Shan Liu, Hong Lu

item.title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
item.description: arXiv:2611.12496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.
item.dc:creator: Jean Maurice Meus, Christian Chapman-Bird, Alberto Vecchio

item.title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
item.description: arXiv:2611.12510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Pad\'e methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.
item.dc:creator: Job Feldbrugge

item.title: Effective Time Advance of Quantum Clocks under Postselection
item.description: arXiv:2611.12609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the familiar twin paradox, the traveling twin ages less than the one who stays behind as a consequence of relativistic time dilation. Here, we show that quantum postselection can effectively reverse this outcome. Using an analytically solvable quantum clock model, we demonstrate that postselection of the center-of-mass motion produces an effective time advance through anomalous weak values, even though every individual motional branch undergoes ordinary time dilation. We extend this analysis to a weak gravitational field and show that an effective time advance can arise even for simple coherent states of the quantum clock motion. We further illustrate this effect using a hydrogen-like atom, revealing how it manifests itself in the atomic wavefunction. Our results demonstrate that quantum interference and postselection can produce an effective time advance beyond conventional relativistic time dilation.
item.dc:creator: Youka Kaku, Akira Matsumura, Tomohiro Fujita

item.title: On Thermodynamic Role of the Gauss-Bonnet Topological Term
item.description: arXiv:2611.12698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the thermodynamic implications of the Gauss-Bonnet topological term in four spacetime dimensions. It has been previously claimed in the literature that this term, although it does not modify the equations of motion, shifts the black hole entropy by a contribution proportional to the Euler characteristic of the horizon. We argue that this conclusion is sensitive to the choice of the boundary action on the horizon. We then identify a choice for which the Wald entropy expression naturally reproduces the Jacobson-Myers entropy, even for non-stationary black holes. We also show that there are no further contributions to conserved quantities from smooth outer boundaries, regardless of the choice of boundary conditions there and of the asymptotic behaviour of the spacetime. Moreover, we demonstrate that the topological Gauss-Bonnet term changes the critical temperature of the Hawking-Page phase transition, opening, in principle, a way for detecting its presence in the gravitational action. In fact, for a positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant, we observe a zeroth-order Hawking phase transition at high temperatures and pressures. While our discussion focuses on the case of the Gauss-Bonnet term in 4D, the results are more general and qualitatively apply to other Lovelock Lagrangians in their respective critical dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Marek Li\v{s}ka, David Kubiznak

item.title: Boundary Formula for Volume Response of Entanglement Wedge Polygons
item.description: arXiv:2611.12715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The vacuum volume of an entanglement wedge polygon is topological. We determine its semiclassical quadratic response to time-symmetric coherent scalar matter in AdS$_3$. A contrast of six interval entropies measures a nonnegatively weighted energy integral, whereas volume depends on the unweighted integral. For negative mass squared above the stability bound, perturbations with the same quadratic coefficient of global energy can match all six vacuum entropies through second order yet have opposite volume responses. A continuum of narrowing quartets reconstructs the volume response with controlled noise. An independent CFT calculation for a dimension-$3/2$ primary reproduces an exact polygon edge formula.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Te Ma

item.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
item.description: arXiv:2611.12772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $\Delta^2_{h,2}/\Delta^2_h\simeq0.04\,\Delta^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $\Delta^2_\zeta=c_w\Delta_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4\epsilon$, and $n_T=-2\epsilon$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $\zeta$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $\Omega_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $\mu$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bertacca, Raul Jimenez, Sabino Matarrese, Mariam Abdelaziz, Marisol Traforetti

item.title: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.12792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $\beta=d\ln m/d\phi$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $\beta_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $\beta_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|\beta|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $\beta_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Sapone, Esteban Arratia

item.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $\mu$-Distortion Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.12861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $\mu$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $\mu$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Shyam Balaji, Bryce Cyr, Sarah R. Geller, David I. Kaiser, Dario L. Lorenzoni, Evan McDonough, Wenzer Qin

item.title: Energy of test objects on black hole spacetimes: A brief review
item.description: arXiv:1207.0887v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we review the issue of defining energy for test particles on a background stationary spacetime. We revisit the different notions of energy as defined by different observers. As is well known, the existence of a time-like isometry allows for the notion of total conserved energy to be well defined. We use this well known quantity to show that a gravitational potential energy can be consistently defined. As examples, we study the case of the exterior regions of an asymptotically flat black hole and of the $\Lambda>0$ Schwarzschild de Sitter case, where an asymptotic region is not available. We then consider the situation in which the test particle is absorbed by the black hole, and analyze the energetics in detail. In particular, we show that the notion of horizon energy as defined by the isolated horizons formalism provides a satisfactory notion of energy compatible with the particle's total conserved energy. With these choices, there is a global conservation of energy. Finally, we comment on a recent proposal to define energy of the black hole as seen by a nearby observer at rest, for which this feature is lost.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Int Jour Mod Phys D24, No. 14 (2015) 1550103
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Corichi

item.title: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
item.description: arXiv:2503.19660v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics for ambient non-zero densities, with the best agreement with GWTC-3 obtained for $\rho_0\sim10^6$ GeV/cm$^3$ and eccentricity $\sim0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Chakravarti, Soham Acharya, Sumanta Chakraborty, Sudipta Sarkar

item.title: On the consistency of non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution
item.description: arXiv:2507.16780v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution obtained by smearing the point sources with a Gaussian distribution. We show that while the form of the metric function and the physical properties derived from that remain valid, not all the components of Einstein equations are satisfied: the angular components fail by exactly the Lorentz force density exerted by the electric field on the smeared charge, which the standard electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor leaves unbalanced. We construct an improved energy-momentum tensor that consistently satisfies Einstein equations. It is the unique conserved completion: the standard Maxwell tensor supplemented by an interaction stress supported on the smeared source. The improved tensor leads to a different prediction for the region where the strong energy condition is violated. For certain choice of parameters, our proposal predicts the violation of the energy condition outside the Cauchy horizon, which might be relevant for the stability of the inner horizon and strong cosmic censorship.
item.dc:creator: Gokhan Alkac, Murat Mesta, Gonul Unal

item.title: Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
item.description: arXiv:2601.03228v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{\lambda \mu}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case. The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams. The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim \eta^{1/2}$, where $\eta$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{\lambda \mu}\|)^{\eta/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $\eta$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion. This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $\eta^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.
item.dc:creator: V. M. Khatsymovsky

item.title: Resummed energy loss in extreme-mass-ratio scattering using critical orbits
item.description: arXiv:2602.10089v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by recent efforts to bridge between weak-field and strong-field descriptions of black-hole binary dynamics, we develop a resummation scheme for post-Minkowskian radiative observables in extreme-mass-ratio scattering, augmented with post-Newtonian terms. Specifically, we derive universal interpolation formulas for the total energy emitted in gravitational waves out to infinity and down the event horizon of the large black hole, valid to leading order in the small mass ratio. We test our formulas using numerical results from direct calculations in black hole perturbation theory. The central idea of our approach is to utilize as a strong-field diagnostic the known form of divergence in the radiated energy along geodesics near the parameter-space separatrix between scattering and plunge. The dominant, logarithmic term of this divergence can be expressed in terms of instantaneous energy fluxes calculated along the unstable circular geodesics that form the separatrix, fluxes that we obtain using interpolation of highly accurate numerical data. The same idea could be applied to bound-orbit radiative observables via either unbound-to-bound mapping or a direct resummation of bound-orbit post-Newtonian expressions.
item.dc:creator: Leor Barack, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather, Oliver Long, Niels Warburton

item.title: A minimal fractional deformation of Newtonian gravity: a unified description of cosmology and weak-field tests
item.description: arXiv:2603.16009v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a minimal fractional deformation of Newtonian gravity as a unified effective framework for cosmology and weak-field gravitational tests. Here we demonstrate that a single-parameter fractional extension of the Newtonian action, motivated by fractal frameworks in field theory with a Stieltjes-type measure, gives rise to an effective framework capable of reproducing gravitational dynamics across vastly different scales. Previous studies of this framework have addressed cosmic evolution, including a nonsingular pre-inflationary phase, an inflationary attractor, radiation- and matter-dominated epochs, and the present accelerated expansion. The evolution of matter density perturbations has also been investigated, with results compatible with cosmological constraints. These applications share a unified effective potential description without introducing additional dynamical degrees of freedom. In this paper, we extend this construction to weak-field gravity, showing that key tests such as the perihelion precession of Mercury and the deflection of light grazing the solar limb are consistently described within the same potential, with all constraints pointing to only a small deviation from standard Newtonian dynamics. These results support a unified effective description of cosmological evolution and weak-field gravity, providing a basis for exploring the smallness of the effective cosmological constant, the hierarchy of Hubble scales, and the Hubble tension.
item.dc:creator: S. M. M. Rasouli

item.title: Classical tests of New General Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2605.05500v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In New General Relativity (NGR), the static spherically symmetric vacuum solution is characterized by two parameters, unlike General Relativity (GR), where the Schwarzschild solution has only one parameter. In this work, using the five classical tests of relativistic gravity (perihelion precession, light bending, Shapiro time delay and de Sitter geodetic precession effect, as well as gravitational redshift), a more stringent constraint on the value of the second parameter was derived compared to the original work [1].
item.dc:creator: V. P. Vandeev, V. A. Parkhomenko, A. N. Semenova, M. A. Matveev

item.title: How much dark matter really matters?
item.description: arXiv:2605.12593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a key probe to trace dark matter. It assumes that mass curves spacetime so that light from a background source is deflected on its way to the observer. If dark matter contributes the major part to a massive cosmic structure, reconstructing the latter from strong-lensing observables allows us to infer characteristics of dark matter. Standard reconstructions fit a pre-defined mass-density model to the data. In this essay, I show how these mass models over-estimate the dark-matter contents of light-deflecting masses. Eliminating these models from the reconstruction reveals that observations directly constrain local properties of light-deflecting masses. How much dark matter is really needed in strong-gravitational-lensing effects and how much do we make up by our model choices?
item.dc:creator: Jenny Wagner

item.title: Inaccessibility of the Schwarzschild Singularity to Quantum Probes
item.description: arXiv:2605.13508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.
item.dc:creator: Vishnulal Cheriyodathillathu, Tanmay Patil, Saurya Das, Soumen Basak

item.title: Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
item.description: arXiv:2605.18625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Ilkka M\"akinen, Hanno Sahlmann, Waleed Sherif

item.title: Collective excitations in quantum gravity condensates
item.description: arXiv:2605.18977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose-Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Calcinari, Adri\`a Delhom, Daniele Oriti

item.title: Electromagnetic duality degeneracy in dynamical black hole mergers
item.description: arXiv:2605.20493v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electromagnetic duality is a symmetry of the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations that rotates electric and magnetic fields while leaving the stress-energy tensor invariant. We present the first fully nonlinear realization of this symmetry in dynamical strong-gravity regimes by performing numerical relativity simulations of charged black hole mergers across a continuous duality family. Starting from electrically charged binaries, we generate dyonic and magnetically charged configurations via duality rotations and evolve them within a common numerical framework. We find that all dual configurations exhibit identical spacetime dynamics, while the emitted electromagnetic radiation is related by a rotation of its polarization equal to the duality angle. Our results demonstrate a degeneracy of gravitational observables under electromagnetic duality and provide a concrete mapping between dual configurations at the level of radiation, establishing electromagnetic duality as an organizing principle for dynamical Einstein-Maxwell solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ferreira, Gabriele Bozzola, Carlos A. R. Herdeiro, Vasileios Paschalidis, Miguel Zilh\~ao

item.title: Red/Blue shifts of photons in a Hayward black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2605.24102v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the red/blue shifts of photons emitted by particles moving along stable circular orbits around a Hayward black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). The PFDM contribution modifies the horizon structure and the characteristic radii associated with circular motion, such as the photon-sphere radius and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). While massive particles follow geodesics of the background spacetime, photon propagation is described by an effective optical metric arising from nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED), which we use to determine the photon sphere and the critical impact parameter. The corresponding redshift and blueshift are sensitive to both the magnitude and sign of the PFDM parameter, providing potentially observable signatures of the surrounding dark matter distribution. Finally, we analyze the black hole shadow and compare its size with observational constraints from Sgr A*. Our results show that positive values of the PFDM parameter decrease the shadow radius, whereas negative values generally lead to larger shadows. The comparison with the observational bounds indicates that only certain negative ranges of the PFDM parameter are consistent with the data, suggesting that black hole shadow measurements can constrain the surrounding dark matter distribution.
item.dc:creator: L. Marlene. L\'opez, L. A. L\'opez

item.title: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars at Finite Temperature
item.description: arXiv:2606.06600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the radial oscillation spectrum of relativistic stars within Israel-Stewart and Navier-Stokes theories, extending previous analyses to include heat diffusion and a thermodynamically consistent finite-temperature equation of state. The inclusion of heat flux gives rise to a distinct thermal sector in the mode spectrum, whose structure closely mirrors the dispersion relations of an infinite dissipative fluid. Within Israel-Stewart theory, the thermal modes transition from purely damped to propagating behavior above a critical overtone number, providing a finite-size realization of relativistic second sound in compact stars. Remarkably, the finite stellar geometry can push even the fundamental thermal mode into the propagating regime -- a feature with no continuum analogue. For the class of equations of state considered here, where finite-temperature corrections enter as controlled, Sommerfeld-type perturbations of a cold polytrope, the thermal sector couples only weakly to the ordinary fluid oscillation spectrum, with the coupling being of second order in a suitable temperature parameter. We further show that the discrete stellar spectrum is well captured by an analytic ansatz constructed from the flat-spacetime dispersion relations, with the star's finite radius discretizing the continuous mode structure. Our results complete the analysis of radial oscillations of viscous stars by incorporating the last remaining dissipative degree of freedom within the Israel-Stewart framework.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Guerrieri, Gabriel S. Rocha, Gabriel S. Denicol, Raissa F. P. Mendes

item.title: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.23862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $\epsilon^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $\epsilon^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $\Xi$, and the quartic horizon function $\Delta_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.
item.dc:creator: Raid M Suleiman, Shanshan Rodriguez, Dominic O. Chang, Leo Rodriguez

item.title: New interpretation of the Minkowski limit of $R^2$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.27799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well-established that the Minkowski limit of pure $f(R)=R^2$ gravity breaks down, unlike that of full Starobinsky theory $f(R)=R+\alpha R^2$. We provide a novel interpretation of this phenomenon using the recent thermal analogy between scalar-tensor gravity and Eckart's relativistic dissipative fluids. In this framework, we show that approaching the Minkowski background corresponds to a diverging effective ``gravitational temperature'' along certain non-stationary FLRW trajectories, while the gravitational temperature remains identically zero along the exact de Sitter family. This perspective naturally rephrases the strong coupling problem as a thermal singularity, demonstrating that $R^2$ gravity departs infinitely far from General Relativity rather than recovering it.
item.dc:creator: Valerio Faraoni, Luca Gallerani, Alain Maltais-Gosselin, Santiago Novoa-Cattivelli, Uri Gorman

item.title: ACT-DR6 consistent inflation in generalised entropic cosmology and $f(Q)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.06582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Within the framework of generalised entropic cosmology and its equivalent $f(Q)$ gravity, we construct inflationary scenarios consistent with recent Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations combined with Planck-BAO data. We work with $f(Q)$ gravity and use the reconstruction scheme from which one can obtain an arbitrary cosmological evolution consistent with desirable theoretical or observational considerations. Explicit inflationary cosmologies of the above theory, which pass ACT-Data Release 6 (DR6) data combined with Planck and BAO, are obtained. For $f(Q)$ gravity coupled with scalar, we obtain ACT inflation for large classes of $f(Q)$ via the choice of the scalar potentials. The entropic cosmology based on generalised entropy, which includes most of the known entropies like Tsallis, R\'{e}nyi, Barrow, etc as a particular case, is investigated. The corresponding FRW equations, depending on the parameters of generalised entropy, are presented. Using the correspondence between the generalised entropy and $f(Q)$ gravity, we obtain generalised entropic inflation, which is consistent with the ACT-DR6. At the next step, the entropic gravity coupled with scalar is considered. It is demonstrated how one can obtain ACT-DR6-consistent inflation for such a theory based on any generalised entropy considered in this paper via the choice of scalar potentials. These findings may point towards the correct unifying entropy of the early universe.
item.dc:creator: Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov

item.title: Post-Newtonian Global Conservation Laws in the Presence of Sensitive Bodies
item.description: arXiv:2607.18145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) approach is the state of the art formalism for performing theory independent tests of weak-field gravity, and for constraining possible deviations from Einstein's theory. Within this framework, global conservation laws are useful for the calculation of dynamics and for giving meaning to parameters. In this paper we extend the concept of semi-conservative and fully-conservative theories of gravity to include situations in which compact astrophysical bodies are modeled as masses that are sensitive to their local environment, as relevant for theories that violate the strong equivalence principle. We find that globally conserved quantities can still exist in the presence of such sensitivities, and find their explicit forms when they do. We identify new ways of writing the coefficients that enter into the PPN metric when a theory of gravity admits conserved quantities in the presence of a sensitive body, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach by comparing it to known results in scalar-tensor theories of gravity.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Clifton, Asta Heinesen, Oliver Pitt

item.title: Quantum Gravity from Fractal Entanglement Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.26035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we explore the possibility that spacetime geometry may emerge from the entanglement structure of an underlying quantum-information network. We develop an exploratory framework, termed Fractal Entanglement Quantum Gravity (FEQG), in which information-theoretic correlations provide a candidate pregeometric structure from which aspects of geometry, quantum dynamics, and gravity may arise. An information-based distance on the correlation graph is considered as a possible means of relating quantum correlations to geometric separation. The framework also investigates whether scale-dependent and fractal properties of the underlying structure could lead to dimensional flow, potentially approaching an effective dimension of two near the Planck scale. Within a scale-relativistic perspective, nondifferentiable trajectories and stochastic descriptions are examined as possible ingredients in an effective quantum dynamics; however, the emergence of the Schr\"odinger equation from the network structure remains to be established. Similarly, the relation between evolving correlations and gravitational dynamics is explored through candidate generalized field equations, while recovering Einstein gravity in an appropriate macroscopic limit remains an open problem. Potential phenomenological consequences include dimensional reduction, modifications to gravitational potentials, and possible deviations from standard quantum mechanics at ultrashort scales. These possibilities are not presented as established predictions, but as directions for further investigation. FEQG thus provides a research program for examining whether quantum-information structure, fractal geometry, and gravitational phenomena can be connected within a common framework.
item.dc:creator: Jaume Gine

item.title: On a cosmological Oppenheimer-Snyder model: matching McVittie and FLRW spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2607.26996v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the necessary and sufficient conditions for the smooth matching of an expanding McVittie spacetime and a spatially flat FLRW spacetime across a general hypersurface: a hypersurface of arbitrary causal character, where the character possibly changes from point to point. We identify and completely characterize a number of special cases. In the general case, we show that the full set of matching conditions is equivalent to a 3-dimensional non-linear system of first order ODEs, subject to a single initial value constraint. Taking the perspective that the McVittie region is specified, we prove a semi-global existence result for this system and interpret these solutions in terms of the physical set-up. Solutions exist and are unique globally to the future. In this direction, the required FLRW spacetime exists and is unique and the matching hypersurface exists almost everywhere and is unique. However, the necessary embedding conditions for the hypersurface necessarily fail at least once - but only at isolated points - along the putative hypersurface. To the past, the matching hypersurface extends to meet the past singularity of the McVittie region. We determine the causal character of the matching hypersurface in these limits, and consider the implications for the existence (or otherwise) of an isotropic source of the McVittie cosmological black hole spacetime. We find that generically, the matching hypersurface has spacelike as well as timelike portions, and so the isotropic region cannot be considered to be an interior for the McVittie exterior. This is in distinction to the Oppenheimer-Snyder model, in which an isotropic dust sphere matches across an everywhere-timelike boundary to the Schwarzschild exterior. On the basis of the sometimes-spacelike nature of the hypersurface, we conclude that an isotropic source of the McVittie spacetime does not exist in a global sense.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Classical and Quantum Gravity, Volume 43, Number 21, (2026)
item.dc:creator: Brien C. Nolan

item.title: How does geometry shape quantum emission in rotating bumblebee gravity?
item.description: arXiv:2608.01398v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compare propagation and static emission estimates in a rotating metric geometry and a stationary metric-affine bumblebee geometry. Their distinct constructions and spatial asymptotics are kept, and normalized Killing times define the physical frequencies and angular velocities. Direct invariant calculations identify the metric-affine outer root and open exterior axes as curvature singularities for generic rotation. The obstruction at bifurcation surface poles concerns the smoothness of the bumblebee field independently. Its mixed meridional component couples angular channels; finite transverse energy fixes the adopted axial condition and defines a self adjoint stationary operator on bounded exterior annuli. For the metric geometry, we construct normalized radiative scalar modes with specified Unruh data, evaluate the horizon frequency transformation, and include spontaneous superradiant emission through the radial scattering map. We prove positivity of the axisymmetric potential and compute numerical transmission factors and a partial scalar energy spectrum alongside an analytical lower bound. The static emission estimates use the stated Stefan-Boltzmann model.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho

item.title: Observational Signatures of Thin Accretion Disks around Rotating Black Holes Embedded in Dark Matter Halos
item.description: arXiv:2608.15487v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Black holes embedded in a dark matter background represent an important candidate model that extends the standard vacuum case, characterizing the strong gravitational environments at galactic centers and the gravitational influence of dark matter. This study focuses on dark matter halo-modified Kerr black holes and systematically investigates the observational characteristics of their surrounding thin accretion disks. The dark matter halo is modeled by a general double power-law density profile, whose integrated mass $M_D(r)$ modifies the radial mass function of Kerr metric to $m(r) = M + M_D(r)$. Based on this spacetime, we analyze the observational properties of their thin accretion disk, including the radiative flux, temperature, differential luminosity, and spectral luminosity as a function of radius, with respect to the black hole spin and dark matter halo parameters. Furthermore, by combining ray-tracing methods, we simulate the bolometric image of the thin accretion disk under different black hole spins, dark matter halo parameters, and viewing inclinations. The dark matter halo enhances the gravitational potential, shifting the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) of the accretion disk outward, suppressing the peak radiative flux, and producing a fainter image, thereby generating signatures that are possibly observational distinguishable from standard vacuum Kerr black holes.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Ying Zhang, Wei-Lun Tong, Tian-Yun Ye, Yong-You Liu, Zhen Li

item.title: First Post-Newtonian Cross Terms in Hierarchical Triple Systems: Multiple-Scale Averaging and its Canonical Consistency
item.description: arXiv:2609.36990v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a two-stage multiple-scale method for hierarchical triple systems, using osculating orbital elements and time as the independent variable. We examine the disputed cross terms at orders $\delta\varepsilon^{3/2}$ and $\delta\varepsilon^{7/2}$, for which the multiple-scale results of Lim and Rodriguez (LR) disagree with the effective field theory results of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST). Here, $\delta$ is the first post-Newtonian (1PN) parameter, and $\varepsilon=a_*/a_2$ ($a_*\simeq a_1$) measures the orbital hierarchy. These terms arise from couplings between relativistic interactions and the tidal field of the third body. Our results agree with KST: there is no secular term at order $\delta\varepsilon^{3/2}$, while the $\delta\varepsilon^{7/2}$ contribution consists of three parts: a direct term, a first-stage coupling between the inner binary's center-of-mass motion and the tidal field, and a second-stage coupling between the 1PN dipole and the quadrupole. Their sum reproduces the inner-orbit secular dynamics generated by KST's magnetic 1PN--quadrupole Hamiltonian, including its exact mass dependence, for nonsingular eccentricities and inclinations in the nonresonant, hierarchical weak-field regime. The analysis includes mean-anomaly perturbations and resubstitution of short-period corrections in both directions. We clarify how the choice of averaging variable affects the normalization of the mean elements and establish agreement with canonical perturbation theory. In particular, osculating and canonical mean elements give the same inner-orbit secular rates at this order.
item.dc:creator: Hideyoshi Arakida

item.title: Post-Newtonian Secular Dynamics of Hierarchical Triple Systems: A Consistent Canonical Treatment of Cross Terms
item.description: arXiv:2610.14505v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the secular Hamiltonian for hierarchical triple systems from the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) three-body Hamiltonian through first post-Newtonian (1PN) order, using Lie--Hori--Deprit canonical perturbation theory and time averaging over the inner and outer orbits. The canonical framework systematically incorporates higher-order cross terms through scalar generating functions and Poisson brackets while preserving the Hamiltonian structure. We recover the electric and magnetic 1PN--quadrupole terms of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST), rather than those reported by Lim and Rodriguez (LR). We further derive the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term, the Newtonian quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian, and a third-order coupling between inner 1PN precession and the squared quadrupole. The outer-pericenter dependence of the quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian is removable by a canonical redefinition of the mean elements. Direct integrations of the Einstein--Infeld--Hoffmann (EIH) equations confirm the de Sitter term, the direct electric term, and the binding-energy renormalization of the inner-binary mass. For the systems considered by LR, the canonical terms do not reproduce the extreme merger acceleration they reported. Instead, the relativistic modulation of the eccentricity cycles is driven primarily by the outer-pericenter-dependent part of the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term.
item.dc:creator: Hideyoshi Arakida

item.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.33883v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Pad\'e approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta

item.title: Unified Black-Hole Interior Dynamics with Small Scalar Input
item.description: arXiv:2610.36129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify a unified dynamical picture connecting small-amplitude scalar input at the event horizon to scalar--Kasner interiors. Within boundary-supported stationary families, area contraction drives the transition from geometric to scalar kinetic dominance. For the Schwarzschild-like branch, the scalar kinetic term remains small but becomes dominant as area contraction suppresses the relative curvature contribution. For the Kerr--Newman-like branch, the scalar kinetic term is strongly amplified as area contraction carries the solution toward the would-be Cauchy horizon. A transition layer then transfers dominance to the kinetic term. The scalar kinetic and geometric terms balance at a positive minimum of the weighted metric diagnostic, explaining inner-horizon loss dynamically. Fully coupled spherical and axisymmetric solutions, including the Reissner--Nordstr\"om and Kerr limits, support this picture. Area contraction provides the physical mechanism, while the would-be Cauchy horizon determines the strength of kinetic amplification and the localization of the transition.
item.dc:creator: Fu-Guo Yang

item.title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.40711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In the sampled configurations, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the ISCO. For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. The resulting image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, Edson Otoniel, Muhammad Israr Aslam, Francisco S. N. Lobo

item.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, Edson Otoniel

item.title: Dimensional dependence of critical phenomena in black hole interiors
item.description: arXiv:2611.00829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Black hole interiors exhibit a critical transition in which a perturbed inner horizon either survives or collapses into a spacelike singularity, but whether the exponent governing this transition depends on spacetime dimension has remained an open question. In this paper, we numerically investigate the interior dynamics of $D$ dimensional Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) black holes perturbed by a real scalar field. Strong perturbations destroy the null inner horizon and produce a spacelike singularity, whereas weaker perturbations preserve it with an areal radius that decreases as the perturbation amplitude increases. As the initial scalar field amplitude $p$ approaches its critical value $p^{*}$, the inner horizon radius decreases continuously to zero. Near criticality, this radius obeys the power law $r_{s}\propto|p-p^{*}|^\gamma$. In four dimensions, different initial scalar field profiles and initial RN black hole charges yield nearly identical critical exponents, $\gamma\simeq1/2$, supporting the universality of the scaling law. Within the investigated range $4\leq D\leq9$, the critical exponent decreases systematically with increasing spacetime dimension. The numerical results suggest the scaling relation $r_s\propto|p-p^{*}|^{1/(D-2)}$. This result establishes a new dimension-dependent universality class for interior black hole critical phenomena, distinct from the standard Choptuik collapse scaling.
item.dc:creator: Li-Jie Xin, Xiangdong Zhang

item.title: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordstr\"om Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.02727v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.
item.dc:creator: Mao-Yuan Wan, Chen Wu

item.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
item.description: arXiv:2611.04750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.
item.dc:creator: Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang

item.title: Excitation factors and exceptional points of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study excitation factors and investigate exceptional points (EPs) of Kerr--Newman quasinormal modes using the exact separated gravitoelectromagnetic equations. At fixed charge, the magnitudes of the excitation factors for the gravitational-led modes studied here decrease with increasing spin, whereas those for electromagnetic-led modes exhibit both monotonic and nonmonotonic behavior. The magnitude of the excitation factor for the first overtone can be comparable to or larger than that for the fundamental mode. We identify 42 EPs at which pairs of modes coalesce in the gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led sectors. Some EPs form sequences involving successive overtone pairs, with higher-overtone pairs coalescing progressively closer to the extremal limit. The additional EPs identified outside these sequences all share the same mode-pair labels as sequence members, but occur at different values of the black hole spin and charge. These findings clarify how rotation and charge shape the relative excitation strengths of different modes and the pattern of mode coalescence in the non-Hermitian spectrum of Kerr--Newman black holes.
item.dc:creator: Jun-Kun Zhao, Tieguang Zi

item.title: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07223v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1100,80]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ waveforms in time with automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 109 SXS evaluation waveforms (106 physical systems), it achieves a mean balanced root-mean-square strain error of 0.0279 and a mean finite-window detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of 0.1190%.
item.dc:creator: Jameson Dong

item.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant Using Strongly Lensed Gravitational Wave Signals
item.description: arXiv:2304.10435v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays an important role in the study of cosmology. In this letter, we propose a new method to constrain the Hubble constant using the strongly lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals. By reparameterizing the waveform, we find that the lensed waveform is sensitive to the $H_0$. Assuming the scenario that no electromagnetic counterpart of the GW source can be identified, our method can still give meaningful constraints on the $H_0$ with the information of the lens redshift. We then apply Fisher information matrix and Markov Chain Monte Carlo to evaluate the potential of this method. For the space-based GW detector, TianQin, the $H_0$ can be constrained within a relative error of $\sim$ 0.3-2\%, using a single strongly lensed GW event. Precision varies according to different levels of electromagnetic information.
