item.dc:creator: Shun-Jia Huang, Yi-Ming Hu, Xian Chen, Jian-dong Zhang, En-Kun Li, Zucheng Gao, Xin-Yi Lin

item.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
item.description: arXiv:2405.01433v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.
item.dc:creator: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu

item.title: Scattering and bound observables for spinning particles in Kerr spacetime with generic spin orientations
item.description: arXiv:2405.09687v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive the radial action of a spinning probe particle in Kerr spacetime from the worldline formalism in the first-order form, focusing on linear in spin effects. We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi

item.title: Atom Interferometer Phase Shear and Spacetime Sectional Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2508.21331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Atom interferometry is a natural laboratory for precision tests of general relativity, but there are no known simple relationships between atom interferometer phase and geometric properties of spacetime. Here we show that a different atom interferometer observable, the phase shear, can be expressed directly as the integrated sectional curvature over a spacetime surface enclosed by the interferometer arms and final beamsplitter, which follows from a generalized Gauss-Bonnet theorem. This interface of quantum mechanics, relativity, and geometry is manifestly coordinate-free and representation-free and can provide a useful computational tool for predicting atom interferometer properties in arbitrary background spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Hunter Swan, Jason M. Hogan

item.title: Spinning States and Unitarity in 3D Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2604.14492v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit the proposal to cure the negative density of states in the three-dimensional gravitational path integral by adding spinning states whose spin scales with the central charge. We show that sub-extremal and extremal spinning states below the black hole threshold can cancel the known negativities, and interpret these states as bulk spinning defects. Additionally, certain overspinning states above the black hole threshold can cure these negativities while preserving the spectral gap. The overspinning states were previously interpreted as classical spinning strings; we instead identify them as overspinning BTZ geometries, which are smooth pure gravity quotients of AdS$_3$ with no fixed points. All of these spinning geometries exhibit causal pathologies in their Lorentzian continuations. Moreover, the overspinning geometries arise from mixed elliptic-hyperbolic identifications and contain a formally real chiral temperature. We also generalize the computation of scalar correlators to the extremal background and propose a quotient-motivated image expression for the overspinning geometries.
item.dc:creator: Ziyi Li

item.title: Eccentric Stellar-mass Binary Black Holes: Population, Detectability, and Waveform Analysis in the LISA and LIGO Era
item.description: arXiv:2605.15265v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Eccentric binary black holes (BBHs) formed through dynamical interactions can significantly contribute to gravitational wave (GW) detections. In this work, we present a simulated catalog of dynamically-formed, stellar-mass BBHs in the local universe, incorporating contributions from the Galactic field (flyby interactions), Galactic nucleus (eccentric Kozai-Lidov evolution), and globular clusters (N-body interactions). Our results predict a wide, highly eccentric BBH population in the Milky Way (MW), with source counts of $\sim 25, 9, 3, 1, <1$ for a 4-year LISA mission and $\sim 36, 13, 5, 2, 1$ for a 10-year mission, at $\mathrm{SNR} > 1, 3, 8, 20, 50$, respectively. Extending this model to cosmological populations, we show that different dynamical channels can produce distinct eccentricity distributions in the LVK band and can contribute hundreds of additional low-SNR mHz sources. Specifically, our model yields a merger rate of $\Gamma \sim 9 \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\sim 150$ extragalactic mHz BBHs with $\mathrm{SNR} > 1$. However, due to the lower mass and weaker GW signals of stellar-mass BBHs, this number declines sharply at higher detection thresholds (e.g., $\sim 1$ for $\mathrm{SNR} > 8$). We further highlight the impact of eccentric BBH signals on the LISA global fit, showing that their individual harmonics can be independently detected in the Milky Way, and may mimic circular binaries with systematically biased chirp masses. Lastly, we show that post-Newtonian waveforms converge reliably for eccentric BBHs with masses of $\lesssim 10^3 M_\odot$ in the mHz band. Overall, eccentric BBHs represent a prevalent and promising target for future space-based GW observatories. The simulated catalog and the LISA Eccentricity Astrophysics Package (LEAP) developed in this work are publicly available at https://github.com/zeyuanxuan/lisa-leap/.
item.dc:creator: Zeyuan Xuan, Smadar Naoz, Kyle Kremer, Michael L. Katz, Bence Kocsis, Erez Michaely

item.title: Loss-Cone-Limited Dark Matter Capture by Early Black Hole Seeds
item.description: arXiv:2606.20964v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid appearance of supermassive black holes at high redshift motivates a reassessment of non-baryonic growth channels. We develop a new loss-cone framework for collisionless dark-matter (DM) capture by early black-hole seeds, with particular attention to phase-space depletion and refilling. The calculation combines Eddington-inverted NFW-like halos, a relativistic direct-capture boundary, and an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of angular-momentum transport. Primordial black holes (PBHs) are treated as massive perturbers whose refilling strength depends on both their abundance and individual mass. Collisionless refilling by triaxial or chaotic centrophilic orbits is included as a phenomenological upper-envelope channel. We show that ordinary stellar relaxation gives negligible DM-driven growth for the fiducial high-redshift seeds. PBH-driven granularity can yield order-of-magnitude growth in sufficiently compact halos, while triaxial or full-loss-cone supply can produce a rapid early burst. In the self-consistent calculations, however, the evolution generally becomes supply-limited. Once the accessible low-angular-momentum phase-space reservoir is depleted, the capture rate collapses and the black-hole mass saturates. Fixed-background NFW calculations therefore overestimate sustained growth, especially in the full-loss-cone limit. A TNG50-calibrated NFW benchmark gives negligible growth even under optimistic refilling assumptions. Collisionless DM capture is therefore unlikely to solve early SMBH growth in generic NFW-like halos, but it can provide a radiatively dark upper envelope in rare compact environments with efficient angular-momentum refilling.
item.dc:creator: Brian Zhang, Grant J. Mathews

item.title: Background-independent one-loop renormalization of tensor and scalar primordial spectra
item.description: arXiv:2607.06042v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jes\'us Gamb\'in Egea, Flavio Riccardi

item.title: Projections and topological classification of black hole thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.07364v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Black hole thermodynamic topology has evolved from classifications based on global topological numbers to more refined schemes including boundary behavior. This development motivates a deeper question: how are different topological manifestations connected within the complete thermodynamic structure? In this paper, we propose the thermodynamic projection conjecture, which seeks to address this question by examining different topological manifestations in the context of the complete thermodynamic structure and exploring their underlying physical connections and formation mechanisms. As a representative application of this idea, we investigate temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions, in which the topological number varies with temperature while the physical parameters are held fixed. We examine how the complete thermodynamic structure gives rise to different topological outcomes on different temperature slices. Our results demonstrate that temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions arise from boundary effects, whereas the pairwise generation or annihilation of equilibrium states in the interior leaves the total topological number unchanged. These results establish that, at fixed physical parameters, the topological differences observed on different temperature slices originate from the same complete thermodynamic structure and can be understood within a unified framework of thermodynamic projections. Furthermore, this study offers a new approach to understanding black hole thermodynamic structures and their rich physical behavior through the interplay between global structures and their local manifestations.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu

item.title: Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
item.description: arXiv:2607.26124v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.
item.dc:creator: Luca Brunelli, Michele Cicoli, Muhammad Hassan, Seyed Ehsan Qoreishi, Francisco Gil Pedro

item.title: Critical and multicritical Kasner scaling in holographic phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2608.04522v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how holographic phase transitions imprint their scaling laws on the local Kasner geometry inside Einstein-scalar black holes. At fixed double-trace coupling, we derive the near-critical scaling of the deviation of the first-epoch Kasner exponent from the Schwarzschild value: $p_t^{(1)}+\frac{1}{3} \propto O^2 \propto (T_c-T)^{1/r}$, where $O$ denotes the boundary condensate and $r$ labels ordinary criticality ($r=1$), tricriticality ($r=2$), and higher multicriticality ($r\geq3$). A super-exponential scalar potential generates a sequence of Kasner epochs separated by scalar-field bounces. We further find that any later epoch that can be tracked continuously across the transition inherits the same temperature exponent, while its coefficient depends on the epoch. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions for the ordinary and tricritical cases. Finally, we show analytically that the leading irrelevant exponent of the infrared fixed point governs the low-temperature Kasner scaling, and verify the resulting scaling numerically for the first Kasner exponent.
item.dc:creator: Ling-Long Gao, Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu

item.title: Luminosity Signatures of Dark Sector Particles from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
item.description: arXiv:2609.24914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Microscopic black holes may form at the centers of neutron stars through the accumulation and collapse of dark matter. While Standard Model particles produced by Hawking evaporation are efficiently absorbed by the dense stellar medium, sufficiently weakly interacting and long-lived particles can escape and subsequently decay into high-energy neutrinos, photons, or charged particles, providing an indirect probe of Hawking radiation. We examine the joint energy--angular distribution of these secondary particles, incorporating mediator propagation, energy-dependent decay, and relativistic decay kinematics. For relativistic mediators, the normalized energy-integrated angular profile becomes approximately independent of the black hole temperature, with its characteristic extent controlled primarily by the combination $c\tau_S/D$ of the mediator lifetime and source distance, as the boost enhancement of the decay length is compensated by relativistic beaming. We demonstrate the viability of this mechanism and illustrate its phenomenology with gravitationally coupled scalars, axion-like particles (ALPs), dark photons, and heavy neutral leptons. Comparing with monochromatic mediator production from dark matter annihilation, we find that the energy-integrated angular profiles can be nearly degenerate, while the energy spectra and energy-resolved angular distributions remain distinct. Although the predicted signals may lie beyond the reach of current observatories, these complementary spectral and angular signatures provide potential targets for future high-energy neutrino and gamma-ray searches.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Dalianis, Anastasios Irakleous

item.title: Relative entropy of entanglement and tripartite minimal surface
item.description: arXiv:2609.38815v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the relative entropy of entanglement for a boundary tripartition $A:B:C$. Our proposal is that, at the leading order, \begin{align} E_R(\rho_{AB}) = \frac{1}{4G_N}\Big[\mathrm{Area}(\Gamma_{\min}) - \mathrm{Area}(\gamma_{AB})\Big] \notag \end{align} where $\Gamma_{\min}$ is the minimal bulk tripartition surface and $\gamma_{AB}$ is the minimal surface homologous to $AB$. For a general random tensor network, we prove the corresponding upper bound by constructing a separable state associated with $\Gamma_{\min}$ and evaluating its relative entropy. We also establish the matching lower bound rigorously for networks of one, two, and three Haar random tensors by bounding the maximal tripartite product-state overlap. In appropriate geometries, the minimal tripartition surface can form a nontrivial tri-junction resembling the Mercedes logo.
item.dc:creator: Takato Mori, Beni Yoshida

item.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13899v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.
item.dc:creator: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat

item.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using a novel multipole re-summation technique, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. This serves as a non-trivial check on our results. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.
item.dc:creator: R. Loganayagam, Avi Wadhwa

item.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.20770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.
item.dc:creator: Debanjan Karan, Babli Khatun

item.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.22614v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

item.title: QRecoupling.jl: numerical and exact computation of classical and quantum recoupling coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.24074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Julia package QRecoupling evaluates classical and quantum recoupling coefficients, such as Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and $3j$ and $6j$ symbols, and user-defined sums of factorial products, with numerical, exact and symbolic targets. One compact factorial rule covers classical and deformed evaluations, while its cyclotomic exponents reveal common factors and determine which terms contribute at unitary levels. Adaptive arithmetic resolves strongly cancelling sums, while exact tests in quantum integers distinguish algebraic zeros from small nonzero values without a computer-algebra system. At spin cutoff 500, classical $3j$ and $6j$ symbols are evaluated about 7 and 15 times faster than with WIGXJPF. For the tested quantum deformations, relative errors remain below $4\times10^{-14}$ through spin cutoff 400. Recurrences compute fusion matrices with 401 channels about 100 times faster than loops over their entries. The resulting coefficients support recoupling identities, changes of coupling basis and tensor-network calculations.
item.dc:creator: Seth K. Asante

item.title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40354v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Ara\'{u}jo, Jo\~ao Gon\c{c}alves, Danny Marfatia

item.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and R\'enyi entropies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40371v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The probe-limit Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. With the scalar mass at the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling at the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase has a closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is the global minimum of the free energy at fixed charge, and linearly stable, as is any nodeless condensate of the model in standard quantization with nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and attenuation of sound are in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it is the lowest state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ within the model, with its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers, from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector, that the superfluid effective theory does not describe. On the hyperbolic black holes that compute charged R\'enyi entropies of a ball, it is a homogeneous hairy phase whose condensate does not fall off toward the entangling surface. With a pinning field there, the phase sets in at R\'enyi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar. Well below a bound on the quartic coupling, the static, homogeneous solutions computed at other couplings and masses keep an infrared fixed point with towers, but not the exact two-fluid law.

item.title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
item.description: arXiv:2610.40769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.

item.title: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
item.description: arXiv:2610.41582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction with two invariant translation ideals, whose complementary quotients yield Galilean and magnetic-Carroll superalgebras. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.
item.dc:creator: Mehmet Ozkan, Utku Zorba

item.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic R\'enyi defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.03413v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The R\'enyi entropies of a ball are computed by the R\'enyi defect (the twist operator viewed as a conformal defect), which in holography is dual to a hyperbolic black hole. We identify hyperbolic black holes with homogeneous charged scalar hair as conformal defects that break the U(1) symmetry. At large $N$ and for repulsive self-interactions, conformality loss of the R\'enyi defect turns explicit symmetry breaking into spontaneous breaking: below a critical index $n_*$ the symmetry-breaking defect is reached only with an explicit source on the entangling surface; at $n_*$ the dimension of a defect operator from a light charged scalar turns complex; beyond $n_*$ the R\'enyi defect flows to the symmetry-breaking defect with no source. The condensate, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, instead preserves them outside a layer at the entangling surface, whose width diverges at $n_*$ with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless scaling. The universal term of the R\'enyi entropy therefore jumps at $n_*$ to that of the symmetry-breaking defect. We demonstrate this mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, with closed-form saddles and defect data, and numerical flows. For a ball we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the radius is large enough, and that it ends at the symmetry-breaking defect as the radius grows.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
item.description: arXiv:2611.08642v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we demonstrate how a Newtonian SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code PHANTOM can be used to estimate the tidal contribution to gravitational wave (GW) waveforms. Using a binary neutron star (BNS) system with typical masses of 1.5 + 1.5 Msun as an example, we show --- by comparing our results with waveforms calibrated against full numerical General Relativity (GR) simulations --- that the tidal contribution to GWs can be reliably extracted using as few as about $10^4$ smoothed particles. Naturally, one must account for the difference in neutron star compactness between Newtonian gravity and GR. At separations greater than $\sim 80$ km, the relative tidal contribution falls below the level of numerical noise inherent in SPH. However, at such distances, GW waveforms for point-like sources are sufficient for detection purposes. It is also crucial to perform a hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation of the initial models; otherwise, the entire GW signal is lost in the numerical noise.
item.dc:creator: Marat Sh. Potashov, Sergei I. Blinnikov, Aleksandra V. Mishakina
